solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird of unusual shape landing on insect

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece lands on top of the second, so it comes before it
something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters of shape are rearranged

parts.note: an ant is a type of insect

explanation.surface: A bird with an odd outline comes down on top of a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of unusual shape' gives PHEAS; in a down entry, 'landing on' puts it above the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed game bird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Fertiliser that Mother couldn't bring from cupboard

definitions.text: Fertiliser that Mother couldn't bring from cupboard

parts.words: Fertiliser that Mother couldn't bring from cupboard
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Old Mother Hubbard went to her cupboard for a bone for her dog but found it bare; the garden fertiliser is ground from animal bones

explanation.surface: A gardener's fertiliser that a mother failed to find in her kitchen cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Mother Hubbard is a British nursery rhyme: she went to the cupboard to fetch her poor dog a bone, but the cupboard was bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground animal bones are sold as a slow-release garden fertiliser rich in phosphate.

clue.text: Letters being sent from distant station?

parts.note: mail being sent is going out
letters are post, the mail

explanation.surface: Asks whether a remote station is where letters get sent from.
explanation.walkthrough: Outgoing letters are 'post out'; read the other way round it gives the remote settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote settlement or military base far from the centre is called a far-flung station of this kind.

clue.text: Find out something from small piece about European Union

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the small piece goes round the union

parts.note: a wisp is a small thin piece, as of hair or straw

explanation.surface: Discovering something from a scrap of paper about the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to realise the truth of a situation is an informal phrasal verb meaning become aware.

clue.text: Cat — one in deep thought about nothing?

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the thinker surrounds the nothing

parts.note: a muser is someone who ponders or meditates
O, the round zero figure, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Asks whether a cat is a deep thinker contemplating nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat kept for catching mice, so it is a kind of cat.

clue.text: Habit that many educated youngsters will acquire?

definitions.text: Habit that many educated youngsters will acquire?

parts.words: Habit that many educated youngsters will acquire?
parts.note: habit here means clothing, as a nun's habit, not a behaviour pattern; pupils put on a set outfit for school

explanation.surface: Wonders what custom many young people pick up through their education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' reads as a learned behaviour; it is the garment sense, as in a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at many schools wear prescribed matching clothes, a garment worn like a nun's habit.

clue.text: One may be seen running round the room

definitions.text: One may be seen running round the room

parts.words: One may be seen running round the room
parts.note: running means extending continuously, as a board fixed along the base of every wall does, not a person jogging

explanation.surface: Someone might be spotted jogging laps of a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests a person moving fast; it means stretching along, as the board at the foot of the walls does.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden strip fixed along the bottom of interior walls extends all the way around a room.

clue.text: One going round Scottish island, say, after tricky term in Oxford establishment

indicators.note: the piece built from one and the island comes after the rearranged term
tricky suggests something awkward and twisted, so the letters of term are rearranged
going round means surrounding, so one encloses the island and the example

parts.note: taken as written
Coll is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland
say signals an example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Someone circles a Scottish island after a difficult term at an Oxford institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges the term, and 'going round' wraps the one about the island and the example. Coll is a small island in Scotland's Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Merton is one of the oldest colleges of the University of Oxford, so it is an Oxford institution.

clue.text: Very small one with wise appearance

parts.note: very in small form, abbreviated, is V
I is the Roman numeral for one
sage means wise

explanation.surface: A tiny person who has a knowing look.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary word for face or countenance, the look a person presents.

clue.text: President needing cutback certain to make strong demand

indicators.note: a cutback trims the word, leaving only its first four letters

parts.note: the full word president, here shortened
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A head of state who requires spending cuts is sure to push hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing cutback' shortens PRESIDENT to its common abbreviation PRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure is forceful insistence or urging, a synonym for a forceful demand.

clue.text: Low state of gloom that doesn't end

indicators.note: a word that does not end has its final letter removed

parts.note: a mood is a fit of sulking or gloominess

explanation.surface: Feeling down in an unending fit of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for low spirits; it is the verb for the noise cattle make.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to make the deep sound of cattle, the same as the verb for a cow's call.

clue.text: After a meal seem not half relaxed

indicators.note: the half word is placed after the a and meal pieces

parts.note: tea is an early evening meal in Britain

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of seem is kept

explanation.surface: Feeling only half at ease after eating.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can be a light meal, not just the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at ease means free from tension or anxiety, so it is a phrase meaning comfortable.

clue.text: Boss in location across US/Canada border

definitions.meaning: a boss is one's senior, higher in rank
the largest of the Great Lakes straddles the border between the United States and Canada

explanation.definitionFit: A superior is someone above you at work; Lake Superior lies on the US-Canadian border.

clue.text: Eastern identity conveyed in religious festival

parts.note: ID is the usual short form of identity, as on an ID card

explanation.surface: An Eastern sense of identity expressed in a holy festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Eid is either of two major Muslim festivals, such as the one marking the end of Ramadan.

clue.text: Drink when international organisation's taken on board France?

indicators.note: taken on board means held inside, so the drink encloses the organisation

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, an international alliance

explanation.surface: A drink while an international body welcomes France aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France' is not the country but the surname of the French novelist, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatole France was the pen name of a Nobel-winning French novelist, so this is his first name.

clue.text: Get round on a river — using this?

definitions.text: Get round on a river — using this?

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Asks what implement you would use to travel about on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes rowing about on a river, and also spells the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole with a flat blade is used to row a boat along water.

clue.text: Badger editor being installed to establish fundamental principles

indicators.note: being installed means placed inside, so the editor goes into the badger

parts.note: brock is an old country name for a badger

explanation.surface: Pester an editor until they're set up to lay down the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the verb meaning pester; it is the animal, BROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrock is the solid rock under soil, used figuratively for the basic underlying principles.

clue.text: Film actor from the Orient given deal?

parts.note: the Orient is the East
deal is fir or pine timber

explanation.surface: A movie star from Asia who is handed a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' suggests a bargain; it is softwood timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Clint Eastwood is an American screen actor and director, famous from Westerns.

clue.text: Grand horse race needs new starter — that's reasonable

indicators.note: the race's first letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: the Grand National is the famous steeplechase run at Aintree

explanation.surface: A big steeplechase wants a new man to start it, which makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known horse race over fences. 'needs new starter' swaps its first letter for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means based on logic and sense, a synonym for sensible or reasonable.

clue.text: Division in religious organisation — then no one turns up

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading upwards, so no and one are written backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A split in a church, after which nobody shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' sends NOI backwards to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a separate part into which something is divided.

clue.text: Stubborn and awkward bod you ultimately esteem

indicators.note: awkward suggests something clumsy and twisted, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of you

parts.note: to rate someone is to esteem them highly

explanation.surface: Someone obstinate and clumsy is still a fellow you hold in esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' shuffles BOD, U and RATE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Last thing you will need — silly nurse not knowing what to do?

indicators.note: the last thing in you is its final letter
silly suggests something muddled, so the letters of nurse are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foolish nurse who is at a loss needs you as a last resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' turns NURSE into NSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undecided or in doubt about how to act is what the word describes.

clue.text: French fashion taken on board by star without delay

indicators.note: taken on board by means held within, so the star holds the fashion

parts.note: an ace is a star performer
ton is French for style or fashion, also used in English for high society

explanation.surface: A celebrity snaps up French couture immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests a celebrity or heavenly body; it is ACE, a top performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, straight away, an idiom for without delay.

clue.text: Come to rest somewhere in Yorkshire

definitions.meaning: to come to rest is to land and stay put
A market town in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to come to rest; Settle is also a market town in the Yorkshire Dales.

clue.text: Trim and quaintly pleasing, almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: cute means attractive in a quaint or endearing way

explanation.surface: Neat and nearly charming in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like an adjective meaning neat; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim something is to shorten it by snipping, a synonym verb.

clue.text: Permit drink after exam success

indicators.note: the drink comes after the exam success

parts.note: a pass is a successful result in an exam
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A glass to celebrate passing a test is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permit' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a travel document.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is an official document authorising travel abroad, a kind of permit.

clue.text: Timber shed maybe at back of court

indicators.note: the shed goes at the back, after the court piece

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
a den is a small retreat or hut, like a garden shed

explanation.surface: A wooden shed perhaps standing at the far end of a tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a sports court; it is the verb to woo. 'Timber' is used adjectivally, as in a timber house.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber house is a house made of wood, so timber used as an adjective means made of wood.

clue.text: Sweet stuff cathedral cook concocted

indicators.note: concocted means mixed up from ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cathedral's cook whips up something sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges the letters of CATHEDRAL and COOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain cocoa-rich confectionery is a kind of sweet treat or candy.
